intro.title: Mini Redux
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simplified version of Redux, a popular state management library, using React and TypeScript. You will learn the core concept of a centralized store that holds the entire application's state, making state predictable and easier to manage. The main technologies involved are React's Context API, TypeScript for type safety, and basic reducer functions to update state. By the end, you'll have a working 'Mini Redux' that demonstrates how to dispatch actions and update state across components.
intro.usecase: State management patterns like Redux are essential in real-world applications where multiple UI components need to share and synchronize data. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard, product filters, shopping cart totals, and user notifications all need consistent state updates. When a user adds an item to their cart, this single action must update the cart icon counter, recalculate totals, and potentially refresh recommendations—all without complex prop drilling. Learning Mini Redux gives you the foundational pattern behind these scalable, predictable state updates in production React applications.
